messages:
sam: FYI pushed a new hit-rate dashboard that breaks prefix cache by context-length buckets (0-128,129-512,512+) and by customer tier. quick link: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/hitrate-context-slices :chart_with_upwards_trend:
anya: Nice. Do we also show per-model and per-route token-saved? we need that to compare kernel/batching changes impact on $$
mike: yep — per-model token-saved column is in the table. also added stacked sparkline for per-route hit-rate over last 7d.
sam: early flag — noticed for model 'redwood-v2-medium' hit-rate drops in 512+ bucket for a handful of top customers. looks correlated with the kernel change rolled on 03/05 (fused-attn tweak).
lee: oof. which customers? can we get a sample trace?
sam: added sample tenant ids in the panel. showing tenant:acme123, tenant:shopio as top regressors. attached one trace in panel (sequence length 700) where batching heuristic switched to large-batch path causing KV lookup miss pattern.
diego: is this kernel-related or batching decision? batching heuristics were updated same day.
mike: from profiling the same trace: kernel selection changed latencies by +8% but that shouldn't affect hit-rate. however batching changed request coalescing window from 4ms -> 8ms for long contexts, and we saw KV cache key formation include trimmed context prefix in runtime v2.2 which caused more distinct keys. so this is a keying regression combined with increased batching window.
anya: TL;DR: more unique keys -> lower reuse -> lower hit-rate -> fewer tokens saved.
rachel: can we compute token-saved delta per-tenant? ops-bot: query job started (job_id=jk-8321) — estimating token-saved delta over last 14 days vs previous 14 days. you'll get results in ~12m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
lee: temporary mitigation: can we relax the prefix normalization so trimmed whitespace and punctuation are ignored? that'll reduce key variance.
diego: also consider reducing batching window back to 4ms for sequences >512 until we fix key derivation.
mike: noted. action items: 1) revert batching window for long contexts (owner: mike) 2) revert the prefix normalization change that added positional markers (owner: sam) 3) backfill hit-rate metrics for fixed-interval comparisons (owner: anya) 4) add unit test for key-stability for common prompt templates (owner: rachel).
sam: added those to the eng-runtime board and set priority P0 for the first two.
anya: small dashboard tweak request: add a per-model normalized hit-rate metric (hit/tokens-eligible) so we account for different prompt sizes.
mike: good idea. also added a column for kernel variant used per-sample so we can correlate kernel selection with hit-rate.
lee: after mitigations, we'll run the perf regression bench (script: scripts/bench_prefix_hits.sh) against canary to confirm token-saved recovers.
rachel: ops-bot results: job jk-8321 finished — summary: tenant-level token-saved delta shows -0.7% overall platform, but -6% for affected tenants. full CSV uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-observability/hitrate/jk-8321.csv
sam: thanks. will push a hotfix to revert the batching window now.
ops-bot: deploy started (deploy_id=d-7782) — target=eng-runtime-canary, user=sam
diego: once canary looks good, schedule a 30m window to roll to prod and monitor the dashboard. I'll prepare an alert if token-saved drops by >1.5% over 10m.
anya: one more long-term note: we should add a small fingerprinting step in the key derivation that hashes normalized prompt templates separately from runtime variables (so prompts with same template map to the same cache key). opened RFC: rfc/prompt-key-template-hash.md
sam: perfect. thanks team. I'll update thread with canary numbers in ~15m. :thumbsup:
